articles.title: Your webhook can arrive twice. Your code should act once.
articles.excerpt: A webhook is a notification, not a promise that your handler will run once. If your application treats every delivery as new work, a retry can repeat an email, an entitlement change, or a provisioning…
articles.body: A webhook is a notification, not a promise that your handler will run once. If your application treats every delivery as new work, a retry can repeat an email, an entitlement change, or a provisioning job. Stripe explicitly documents that webhook endpoints can receive the same event more than once. That does not mean Stripe charges a customer again whenever it repeats a notification. Receiving an event and initiating a payment are different operations. This article is about what your application does after receiving the notification. The useful design question is simple: if this work runs again, what happens? A receipt is not a completed job Consider an illustrative SaaS application. A verified billing event arrives, and the application needs to update a local entitlement record.

articles.title: Apache HBase web UIs separate authentication from sensitive administration
articles.excerpt: Apache HBase web UIs separate authentication from sensitive administration Apache HBase exposes web interfaces for the master, region servers, and related services. These pages provide cluster state,…
articles.body: Apache HBase web UIs separate authentication from sensitive administration Apache HBase exposes web interfaces for the master, region servers, and related services. These pages provide cluster state, configuration, table metadata, and operational actions. HBase's own security model says such information is expected to be available only inside a trusted network perimeter. That expectation is a deployment assumption, not an automatic control. The HBase Web UI can use SPNEGO or LDAP authentication. Its documentation also describes an administrator list for sensitive endpoints. A user who passes authentication can still be limited by the admin configuration for operations that change or expose more detail. The model distinguishes ordinary UI access from access to privileged functions.

articles.body: When a site drops to a bare page reading Error establishing a database connection , WordPress has already given up: it never reached the point where it could load a theme, so the screen you see is the last thing PHP could print. The quickest way to fix a WordPress database connection error is to stop reading that screen and start reading the four constants that produced it. Below are the three realistic routes to those constants, when each one fits, and a full build of the one that hands you the real MySQL error instead of a generic failure. Three routes to the same four constants, and only one of them tells you why Every fix ends in the same place: a working DB_NAME , DB_USER , DB_PASSWORD and DB_HOST in wp-config.php .

articles.body: AI agents are becoming increasingly capable of reasoning, planning, analyzing information, and executing multi-step tasks. But there is one important challenge: How does an AI agent actually interact with the real web? An LLM can generate a search query, understand instructions, summarize information, and decide what to do next. However, interacting with a modern website often requires more than generating text. It may require opening a browser, navigating to a URL, waiting for JavaScript to load, clicking buttons, filling out forms, scrolling through pages, extracting information, and handling dynamic website content. This is where browser infrastructure becomes an important part of AI agent development.

articles.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
articles.excerpt: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility.
articles.body: A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact Explanation: Don’t judge a galaxy by its size. Our home galaxy, the Milky Way , is about 100,000 light years across. This huge expanse of space contains hundreds of billions of stars! The smallest galaxies, called dwarf galaxies , are about 1/10th the size of the Milky Way and only contain a few billion stars. They are also the most common type of galaxy in the whole universe.
